pairs.why: A's spur is held on by a strap around the ankle and the boot has pull loops and a normal shaft, while B's spur sticks straight out of the heel with nothing holding it and the shaft is stretched and leaning.
Both tables and stools stand solidly on the grass; B's checkerboard is closer to a playable 8x8 grid, while A's board has too many small squares.
B's lifebuoy hangs from a hook on its post and the deck sits squarely on its piles, while A's ring floats loosely in front of a post and the rope runs across the deck to it.
A is a wall clock lying flat against the wall with a matching shadow, like the real card, while B is a round clock standing on its rim on a ledge with no stand to stop it rolling.
B's keys have digits and operator signs laid out like the real calculator, while A's keypad is blank square buttons that could not be used.
A's cat sits naturally, with its legs, tail and belled collar all attached, while B's body is a stiff figurine shape with tiny front legs and a collar that floats like a separate ring.

A's pier runs from the beach on solid posts and its lifebuoy hangs on a rope from a post, while B's lifebuoy sits on top of a post in the middle of the deck and its reflection floats in open water far from the pier.
The two wagons are almost identical, both with small front wheels, large rear wheels, a tongue and a canvas cover on one consistent frame, so neither is built better.
